newsitem.title: USA: Best puts Blue Cross of Ohio unit under review.
newsitem.headline: Best puts Blue Cross of Ohio unit under review.

text.p: A.M. Best Co said on Tuesday it has placed the "A-" (Excellent) rating of Medical Life Insurance Co, a unit of Blue Cross & Blue Shield Mutual of Ohio, with negative implications.

The rating reflects the weak financial position of Medical Life's parent company and the ownership uncertainties surrounding Medical Life after the Ohio Department of Insurance placed a supervisory order on Blue Cross, A.M. Best said.
A.M. Best said the order follows Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Ohio's reported $95 million loss in 1996, which reduced reserves below minimum required state levels.
Also, the insurer was notified that insurance regulators intend to disapprove of a plan to sell itself to Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, A.M. Best said.
The Ohio Department of Insurance is attempting to resolve management control issues at Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Ohio, the company said.
The supervisory order puts the state Department of Insurance in control of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Ohio, with state regulators on site to ensure that the company continues to run effectively.
This rating action follows the lowering of Medical Life's rating to "A-" (Excellent) in December 1996, A.M. Best said.
